surface: text-CHECK pseudo-enums vs real Postgres enums (exhaustiveness coverage)
claim: The schema uses two different mechanisms for closed value sets and only one of them can be checked at compile time. FIVE real Postgres enums (app_role, application_status, auto_tip_mode, job_category, job_status) generate into types.ts as string unions PLUS a runtime Constants array, which is what lets src/test/jobStatusExhaustive.test.ts enumerate job_status from its source of truth and assert every label/colour map covers every member. surface: public.user_roles RLS: 'Deny all deletes to user_roles' is a PERMISSIVE no-op
claim: user_roles carries a policy named 'Deny all deletes to user_roles' with USING (false), but it is declared PERMISSIVE, not RESTRICTIVE. Permissive policies are OR-ed together, so a permissive USING(false) contributes nothing at all: it can never subtract access. DELETE on user_roles is therefore governed entirely by the sibling 'Admins can delete roles' policy, exactly as if the deny policy did not exist. The current net behaviour is probably the intended one (admins may delete roles), so this is not an open hole -- it is a security control that reads as a hard stop, is named as a hard stop, and enforces nothing. That is the 'configured but does nothing' class, and on the table that grants admin. Note the contrast with its twin: 'Deny all updates to user_roles' is also permissive-false, but it happens to be the ONLY permissive UPDATE policy on the table, so updates really are denied -- by the absence of any passing policy, not by the deny. Two policies written the same way, one working by accident and one inert. Routed to lh-authz-rls as the owning lane.
repro: SELECT polname, polcmd, polpermissive, pg_get_expr(polqual, polrelid) FROM pg_policy WHERE polrelid='public.user_roles'::regclass on prod fncmgoasalhdgfwzhsqa returns 6 rows. polcmd='d': 'Admins can delete roles' PERMISSIVE USING has_role((SELECT auth.uid()),'admin'), and 'Deny all deletes to user_roles' PERMISSIVE USING false. polcmd='w': only 'Deny all updates to user_roles' PERMISSIVE USING false WITH CHECK false. No RESTRICTIVE policy exists on the table.

claim: Both sites drop the Supabase error and then check ONLY the zero-row case — which means the case they were written to catch is the one they miss. surface: post-job checkout window → captured amount vs jobs.budget
claim: jobs.budget stays poster-writable while payment_status='unpaid' (enforce_poster_jobs_money_lock only locks once funded — verified live via pg_get_functiondef on prod), and the Stripe Checkout line items are frozen at session creation. A poster who edits budget between create-payment's session creation and paying is charged the OLD amount while every downstream payout computes from the NEW jobs.budget. Inflation is caught only because payouts link source_transaction (transfer > charge is rejected by Stripe) — but that link is best-effort inside a try/catch (process-scheduled-payouts:539-550 'Could not link charge' warn-and-continue), so a transient Stripe read failure turns the cap off and the inflated transfer draws from the platform balance. Deflation (lower budget after session creation) silently over-charges the poster with no reconciliation. Nothing at funding time compares pi.amount_received against budget+fees.
repro: Live: pg_get_functiondef(enforce_poster_jobs_money_lock) on prod shows the funded-only gate; code: create-payment/index.ts:420-435 freezes line items, checkoutSessionCompleted.ts:651-744 records funding without amount reconciliation, process-scheduled-payouts/index.ts:539-550 best-effort source_transaction.

note: REFINED after reading release-payout: that path already hard-caps payout at pi.amount_received (release-payout/index.ts:561-596) and documents this exact budget-edit hazard. Residual gap: (a) process-scheduled-payouts has NO explicit captured-amount cap — only best-effort source_transaction inside try/catch — so the two payout paths disagree on a guard both need; (b) the funding webhook never reconciles captured vs budget, so poster-deflation over-charge remains invisible. Fix: add the same cap to process-scheduled-payouts.

surface: charge-recurring-visits → Stripe Tax transactions never registered + fee floor excludes tax

surface: CI / git hooks / cron — types.ts freshness enforcement
claim: NOTHING enforces types.ts freshness. Zero references to 'gen types', 'db:types' or 'types.ts' exist across all 24 .github/workflows files, .husky/pre-commit, or the lint-staged config. This is the root cause of SI-012 and of GD-001: a migration can drop NOT NULL, deploy green via db-deploy.yml, and leave the compiler asserting a withdrawn guarantee indefinitely. db-drift-detect.yml does NOT close this gap - it compares migration VERSION LISTS (repo filenames vs prod schema_migrations), so a migration present in both sides reports zero drift while types.ts is arbitrarily stale. surface: iOS springboard app-icon badge / APNs payload
claim: The app-icon badge can never change while the app is closed, so it diverges from server unread state in exactly the case a badge exists for. Three independent causes, all verified: (a) no caller anywhere sets payload.badge, so aps.badge is never present in any push APNs delivers — send-push-notification/index.ts:161 emits it only when 'typeof payload.badge === number', and a grep for 'badge' across all of supabase/functions/ returns zero hits outside that file; (b) appBadge.ts drives the badge from the running app only (useNavUnreadCount), so it is frozen at whatever value the last foreground session left; (c) no PushNotifications.presentationOptions is configured, so PushNotificationsHandler.willPresent returns [] and even a foreground push updates nothing.

Read node_modules/@capacitor/push-notifications/ios/Sources/PushNotificationsPlugin/PushNotificationsHandler.swift:36-58: willPresent returns [] when getConfig().getArray('presentationOptions') is nil, and capacitor.config.ts declares no PushNotifications plugin block at all.

surface: db: cron_run_log / cron_work_expectations coverage across all 44 pg_cron jobs
claim: HALF THE CRON FLEET HAS LIVENESS MONITORING ONLY — NO WORK VISIBILITY AT ALL. Of the 44 scheduled pg_cron jobs, 22 are SQL crons (`SELECT public.fn()`) and NONE of them has ever produced a single row in cron_run_log — that table is fed exclusively by sweep_silent_cron_failures ingesting net._http_response, so a SQL cron's return value is written nowhere and read by nothing. pg_cron's own job_run_details records only 'succeeded' and '1 row'. Correspondingly, every one of those 22 jobs is registered in cron_work_expectations with candidate_key = NULL, and sweep_silent_cron_failures filters `WHERE c.candidate_key IS NOT NULL` — so the app's silent-work detector skips all 22 BY CONSTRUCTION. The app can prove these jobs FIRED; it cannot in any way tell whether they DID ANYTHING. That is exactly the failure mode cron_work_expectations was built to catch. The affected set includes money- and safety-adjacent sweeps: sweep-release-last-chance (the last-chance-before-escrow-auto-releases warning), detect-stuck-payments, reap-stranded-instant-payouts (which exists because instant payout has stranded money before), auto-start-due-jobs, sweep-dayof-confirm-reminders, sweep-no-show-alerts, sweep-expired-auto-bans and sync-profiles-update-grants. Each of these returns a work count (integer or jsonb) that is discarded at the call site.

claim: AUTO-TIP IS THE ONE MONEY CRON WHOSE BACKLOG DOES NOT DRAIN — a >24h outage loses every tip in the gap, permanently and silently. auto-tip-charge runs hourly and calls auto_tip_candidates(_since_hours := 24), whose predicate is 'j.updated_at > now() - make_interval(hours => 24)'. That is a hard exclusion, not a page window: a job whose completion falls outside the last 24 hours can never be picked up again by any run, and no other code path charges an auto-tip. So if the cron (or pg_cron itself — a 65-minute total dispatch blackout already occurred on 2026-09-01) is down for more than a day, every poster who opted into auto-tip silently does not tip and every helper is silently under-paid, with no queue, no retry and no record that anything was skipped. The window buys nothing: idempotency is already provided by the separate, permanent guard 'NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tips t WHERE t.job_id = j.id AND t.source = ''auto'')', so widening _since_hours cannot cause a double-charge. surface: Cold launch — splash safety net vs the keychain hydrate cap
claim: The splash-screen safety net is armed downstream of the very thing it exists to protect against, so its stated guarantee does not hold. nativeInit.ts ends with a module-scope setTimeout(hide, 1500) commented 'if something hangs in initNative(), force-hide the splash after 1.5s so the app can never be stuck'. But main.tsx imports App.tsx on line 2 and nativeInit on line 4, and App.tsx pulls in integrations/supabase/client.ts, which does a TOP-LEVEL 'await hydratePromise' on native (client.ts:28) worth up to HYDRATE_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000ms of Capacitor Preferences bridge I/O. ES module evaluation therefore completes that 2s await BEFORE nativeInit.ts evaluates and arms the timer. Two consequences: (a) worst-case time from launch to a GUARANTEED splash hide is ~3.5s (2000 hydrate + 1500 net), not the 1.5s the comment implies; (b) the net provides no cover at all for a hang during hydration, which keychainStorageAdapter.ts:22-26 explicitly names as 'a real state' since these are the earliest bridge calls in the WebView lifecycle. The 2000ms internal cap on hydrate is what actually bounds that window; the splash net contributes nothing to it. Bounded and non-fatal, but the invariant asserted in the comment is not the one the code provides.

surface: Global — every .liquid-glass/.glass-* frosted surface (login/signup card, top nav, sticky headers, chat composer dock, every Dialog/AlertDialog via .glass-modal, form field glass, skeleton loaders)
claim: The app's entire frosted-glass design language renders with ZERO backdrop blur for every Chromium-based visitor (desktop Chrome/Edge, and the Android Capacitor WebView) in the PRODUCTION build. Only WebKit/Safari/iOS gets the intended blur. This is the mirror image of the already-fixed reduce-transparency minifier bug documented in CLAUDE.md: that fix special-cased ONE rule pair behind an @supports guard, but every OTHER backdrop-filter pair in src/index.css (11 rules: .glass, .glass-nav, .glass-nav.is-scrolled, .liquid-glass, .tracker-merged>.liquid-glass, .glass-header, .glass-dock, .glass-modal, .glass-field, the :has() adornment override, .skeleton-glass — src/index.css:1290,1732,1751,1876,1929,1942,1965,1979,2006,2026,2343) still writes 'backdrop-filter: X; -webkit-backdrop-filter: X;' as a plain sequential pair with no @supports boundary. Vite's CSS minifier collapses the pair and keeps only the LAST-declared one — and in source the unprefixed comes first, -webkit- second, so the minifier drops the unprefixed 'backdrop-filter' and ships '-webkit-backdrop-filter' alone. Confirmed empirically that Chromium does NOT apply blur from a bare -webkit-backdrop-filter declaration with no unprefixed twin (getComputedStyle reports the effective 'backdrop-filter' as literal 'none'), while WebKit still applies it because WebKit aliases the two. On the DEV SERVER (unminified) both properties survive and both engines render correctly — this is a build-only defect, invisible unless you check dist.

surface: useKeyboardInset — keyboard avoidance on Messages, PostJob, ProfileEditForm, BrowseSearchBar, FilterSheet
claim: The hook reads as an either/or and behaves as a both: on NATIVE it attaches the Capacitor Keyboard listeners AND the visualViewport listeners at the same time. The Capacitor branch lives inside an async IIFE that is never awaited, and its early 'return' exits only that IIFE — not the useEffect callback — so the visualViewport block below it runs unconditionally, on every platform, plus a synchronous update() call. Both then write the same piece of state. The comment on the catch says 'plugin not available — fall through to visualViewport', which is the intended behaviour and is not what the code does. The conflict is real rather than merely redundant because capacitor.config.ts sets Keyboard.resize = 'body': when the keyboard opens the WebView body is resized, so window.innerHeight shrinks with it and update() computes diff ~= 0 and calls setInset(0) — overwriting the true keyboardHeight the Capacitor listener just set. Which value survives depends on event ordering. Five keyboard-critical surfaces consume this hook. It survived because the unit tests mirror the INTENDED split: there are native-subscribes tests and web-subscribes tests, and not one asserts that the native path does NOT also subscribe to visualViewport.
repro: Read src/hooks/useKeyboardInset.ts:19-60. The 'return' at the end of the 'if (Capacitor.isNativePlatform())' block sits inside '(async () => { ... })()', so it returns from the async function; the IIFE is invoked without await, so control continues synchronously to 'const vv = window.visualViewport' and the addEventListener/update() calls below. Cross-check capacitor.config.ts plugins.Keyboard.resize = 'body'. Then src/hooks/useKeyboardInset.test.tsx: the 10 cases split cleanly into 'native:' and 'web:' groups with no case covering both at once. CAVEAT: the double-subscription is certain from JS semantics; which writer wins, and therefore the visible severity, needs a device — I could not build for the simulator (iOS platform component missing).

claim: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is written to the function log on every invocation, and every configured signing secret is written on every signature failure. index.ts:64 logs webhookSecret.slice(0,8) plus its exact length unconditionally at the top of the handler; index.ts:153 logs, for EACH comma-separated secret, slice(0,8) and exact length. Stripe signing secrets are prefixed 'whsec_' (6 chars), so slice(0,8) publishes 2 characters of real entropy plus the exact length of each secret - not enough to forge a signature on its own (90+ bits remain), which is why this is LOW and not higher. It is still a signing secret written to a log on every request: Supabase function logs are visible to anyone with dashboard access and are shipped to any configured log drain, so the secret's blast radius becomes 'everyone who can read logs' rather than 'the function runtime'. index.ts:61 logs stripeKey.slice(0,8), which is harmless by comparison - 'sk_live_' / 'sk_test_' is exactly 8 characters, so it reveals only the mode the line says it is revealing, and is worth keeping. Fix is confined to my lane and to one file: drop the prefix/length from :64 and :153, keep the count and the mode. Everything else about this function's verification is correct - it fails closed (a forged or unsigned event returns 200 to stop Stripe retries but never reaches a handler), it supports multiple endpoint secrets, and it has an idempotency guard.

surface: db: the four cron detectors (sweep_cron_http_failures / sweep_silent_cron_failures / sweep_dead_crons / sweep_cron_blackouts)
claim: THE FOUR CRON DETECTORS DO NOT DUPLICATE EACH OTHER — but sweep_dead_crons is the sole watcher of the other three and has no watcher of its own. Answering the orchestrator's question directly: there is NO overlap. The four read different inputs, emit different verdicts, write different error_logs sources, and are deliberately staggered. sweep_cron_http_failures (*/15) reads net._http_response status codes and catches an edge function answering non-2xx -> 'cron-http'. sweep_silent_cron_failures (:47) reads cron_run_log bodies against cron_work_expectations.candidate_key and catches a 2xx that found candidates and dispositioned none -> 'cron-silent'. sweep_dead_crons (:53) reads cron.job_run_details against expected_max_gap and catches unscheduled / inactive / never-ran / dead / erroring -> 'cron-dead'. sweep_cron_blackouts (:57) differences the AGGREGATE cron.job_run_details dispatch stream for holes >15 minutes and catches pg_cron itself dispatching nothing -> 'cron-blackout'. Four distinct failure modes, no redundancy. THE REAL RISK IS TOPOLOGICAL, NOT DUPLICATION. All four detectors are themselves pg_cron jobs, and only ONE thing can notice a detector failing: sweep_dead_crons, which is the only function in the entire 254-function catalog besides the read-only reporter cron_dispatch_health() that reads expected_max_gap. So sweep_dead_crons watches the other three — and nothing watches sweep_dead_crons. If it stops firing or starts raising, the database emits no signal of any kind, and the failure of every other detector becomes simultaneously unobservable. Compounding it, sweep_dead_crons is blind to intermittent failure (CJ-004), which is the LIVE state of sweep_silent_cron_failures: 3 raises, 0 cron-dead rows. This is the exact shape of CJ-009 in the CI half — schedule-heartbeat.yml also watches everything except itself — so the same structural gap exists independently on both sides of the stack.
repro: PROD fncmgoasalhdgfwzhsqa, 2026-09-02 18:20 UTC. 1) Sole reader: select p.proname from pg_proc p where p.pronamespace='public'::regnamespace and pg_get_functiondef(p.oid) ilike '%expected_max_gap%' => exactly two rows, 'cron_dispatch_health' and 'sweep_dead_crons'. cron_dispatch_health is a read-only reporter with no INSERT and no net.http_post — it raises no alarm — so sweep_dead_crons is the only ACTOR. 2) No duplication: pg_get_functiondef on all four confirms the distinct inputs above; cron.job shows the stagger '*/15 * * * *', '47 * * * *', '53 * * * *', '57 * * * *'. 3) error_logs sources are disjoint in practice: select tags->>'source', count(*) from error_logs where tags->>'area'='cron' group by 1 => cron-http 126 rows across 7 jobs, cron-dead 1 row (payment-confirm-reminder), cron-silent 0 rows ever, cron-blackout 0 rows. 4) The live blind spot, and the one nuance that softens it: select jobname, last_status, recent_failures from public.cron_dispatch_health() where recent_failures > 0 => a SINGLE row, sweep-silent-cron-failures with recent_failures = 2 — it is the only job in the fleet with any failures, and cron_dispatch_health DOES expose it. But that function is read by exactly one caller, src/components/admin/adminHealth/useCronHealth.ts, i.e. a passive tile on /admin?view=health. No Slack, no error_logs row, no push. A human must open that page. Same passive-tile shape as CJ-006's DLQ count.

claim: RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET is NOT SET in the deployed prod environment, so resend-webhook refuses EVERY Resend delivery with 503 and has never ingested a single bounce or complaint. The platform is actively sending mail (171 emails all-time, 160 in the last 30 days, most recent 2026-09-02 18:24Z) into a suppression list that has 0 rows. Consequence: hard-bounced addresses keep being mailed and spam complaints are never honoured, which is precisely how a sending domain's reputation degrades - and the mail that then starts landing in spam includes password resets, email verification and payment receipts, i.e. the auth channel. Resend will also retry a 503 and can disable a persistently failing endpoint outright. Nothing surfaces this: the missing-secret branch does console.error and returns 503 with NO postSlackOpsAlert, unlike stripe-webhook's equivalent branch which does alert. This is the SECOND time this exact function has been silently dead - its own header comment documents the first (a Fetch Headers vs plain-object bug that made it 401 every delivery, found only after the fact), and config.toml's comment names the empty suppressed_emails table as 'the exact state that made both suppression guards no-ops'. The code itself is correct and fails closed by design; the defect is purely that the secret was never provisioned. FIX IS OUTSIDE THE REPO: supabase secrets set RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_... for project fncmgoasalhdgfwzhsqa, taken from the Resend webhook endpoint's signing secret. That is an owner action - I cannot mint the secret. Filed HIGH but NOT --blocker: it degrades deliverability progressively rather than breaking a launch-day flow, though a verifier who weights the auth channel may reasonably upgrade it.
repro: Live prod probe, provably non-mutating - the missing-secret check is the FIRST thing after the method check, so no body is read and no DB call is made: curl -X POST https://fncmgoasalhdgfwzhsqa.supabase.co/functions/v1/resend-webhook -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{}' -> HTTP 503 {"error":"Webhook signing secret not configured"}. The function's own code makes this a clean discriminator: index.ts:90-96 returns 503 'Webhook signing secret not configured' when RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, and index.ts:139-142 returns 401 'Invalid signature' when it IS set but the signature is bad. A 503 therefore proves the secret is absent from the deployed environment, not that my request was malformed. Corroborating prod SQL: SELECT count(*) FROM suppressed_emails -> 0; SELECT count(*) FROM email_send_log -> 171 total, 160 in 30d, max(created_at) 2026-09-02 18:24:12Z. Gateway is NOT the obstacle - config.toml correctly sets verify_jwt=false for this function and an unauthenticated GET reaches the handler (405 'Method not allowed'), so the 503 is the function's own answer.

surface: Activity → posted/applied job card → Review chip (PostedJobActions.tsx:781, AppliedJobCard.tsx:511)
claim: The Review chip is offered forever; the server stops accepting reviews after 30 days, and the client has no idea. The live INSERT policy 'Users can create reviews for eligible jobs' on public.reviews requires COALESCE(poster_completed_at, helper_completed_at, updated_at) > now() - interval '30 days' AND (has_active_dispute = false OR dispute_resolved_at IS NOT NULL). The client gate is only payment_status: canReview = job.payment_status === 'released' || 'payout_pending' (PostedJobActions.tsx:725-726) and the same on the helper side (AppliedJobCard.tsx:511). grep of src/ finds NO 30-day review constant anywhere and no has_active_dispute check on the helper side. So a job that crosses 30 days keeps a live Review chip: the user taps it, writes the review, submits, and gets 'We couldn't post your review — this job may no longer be open for reviews. Refresh and try again.' (ReviewForm.tsx:206-208). Refreshing can never help — the window is closed permanently. Every completed job crosses this line eventually, so the population of offer-then-refuse jobs only grows. surface: mapkit-token → unauthenticated minting of UNRESTRICTED Apple MapKit JS tokens
claim: mapkit-token mints a real, Apple-signed, one-hour MapKit JS token to anyone who asks, with no authentication (verify_jwt=false), NO RATE LIMIT of any kind, and no origin binding whenever the caller simply omits the Origin header. originClaimFor() returns null when there is no Origin header and the payload is built as 'if (origin) payload.origin = origin' (index.ts:89-91, :136), so the claim is absent rather than defaulted. Omitting a header is the trivial case for any non-browser client. The result is that an unauthenticated script can mint unlimited domain-unrestricted tokens against this Apple developer account (team P85MCK558V), each usable on any site for an hour, consuming the account's MapKit JS daily map-view quota - which when exhausted breaks the map for real users and is billable past the free tier. The code comment at :82-88 is honest about WHY the no-Origin path exists (the native WebView sends no web origin), so the omission is deliberate and the trade-off is understandable; the defect is that nothing bounds it. What is NOT honest is the security justification in supabase/config.toml, which argues verify_jwt=false is safe because 'The token this mints is locked to the requesting origin ... so a token obtained without a session only works on this app's own domain'. That is false for exactly the easiest path to take, so the stated basis for making the endpoint public does not hold. Suggested fix, entirely in my lane: bound it (rate limit per IP, or require an authenticated caller when Origin is absent), and correct the config.toml comment to describe what the code actually does. NOTE this function does NOT import _shared/rate-limit.ts, so this is not a duplicate of the already-filed rate-limit defect - it is the absence of any limiter at all.

Base64url-decoding the returned JWT gives HEADER {"alg":"ES256","kid":"4QA8J9TA8K","typ":"JWT"} and PAYLOAD {"iss":"P85MCK558V","iat":1788373624,"exp":1788377224} - note there is NO 'origin' claim, i.e. the token is domain-unrestricted. Repeated calls return fresh valid tokens with no throttling and no 429. surface: Password reset + signup confirmation on native — /reset-password and /account-pending cannot be claimed as Universal Links
claim: RESTATES the retracted OPEN_ITEMS item 7 (see NB-012) as the defect that is actually live. The hash is no longer the blocker; the session-construction ORDER is, and it is a worse bug because it dead-ends the user at the last possible moment. supabase-js reads the URL fragment only inside detectSessionInUrl, which runs ONCE at client CONSTRUCTION. On native the client is built at app boot from capacitor://localhost/ with no fragment — long before appUrlOpen delivers the link. So if /reset-password were claimed in the AASA, the recovery tokens would arrive in window.location.hash, ResetPassword.tsx:79-80 would read type=recovery and set ready=true, the form would render, the user would type a new password, and ONLY THEN would supabase.auth.updateUser({password}) fail with 'Auth session missing'. CURRENT STATE IS SAFE: both paths are explicitly excluded in the AASA and the reset works in the browser, so nothing is broken for users today. This is filed HIGH because it is a live constraint on the auth surface, the exclusions are the only thing preventing it, and the AASA comments are the sole place the reasoning is recorded — a future lane 'helpfully' claiming those two paths would ship an account-recovery dead end. PRECONDITION FOR CLAIMING THEM: ResetPassword must parse access_token/refresh_token out of the fragment and await supabase.auth.setSession() (or verifyOtp) BEFORE rendering the form, and AccountPending must do the same. Neither does today.

surface: calculate-tax → unauthenticated, unmetered Stripe Tax API spend
claim: calculate-tax is public (verify_jwt=false, deliberately - it is the post-a-job pricing preview shown before a session exists) and has NO rate limiting of any kind, yet every accepted request performs a BILLED third-party call: stripe.tax.calculations.create (index.ts:66). Stripe charges per tax calculation, so an unauthenticated caller can drive unbounded spend on the account's Stripe Tax bill by looping the endpoint with a valid-shaped body. Reaching the Stripe call is cheap: the only guards are budgetCents finite and > 0 (index.ts:48), zip present and a string (:51), and isLaborTaxable(category) (:60) - no session, no origin check, no throttle. The function's header is right that it creates nothing and holds no money, and config.toml's reasoning for making it public is sound on the data-exposure axis ('the worst a caller can do is learn the sales tax on an amount in a ZIP, which is public information'). But that reasoning only covers information disclosure; it does not cover COST, and cost is the exposure here. Same defect class as EF-007 (mapkit-token) - a public endpoint whose per-request work is billed by a third party, with the security argument written only about data. Note this is NOT a duplicate of the already-filed _shared/rate-limit.ts defect: calculate-tax does not import that module at all, so this is the absence of a limiter rather than a weak one. Fix is in my lane: add a per-IP throttle, and/or cache calculations by (budgetCents, zip, category) since the same three inputs always yield the same answer - a cache would cut both the bill and the abuse ceiling. brand-asset, contact-support and ai-job-builder, the other public endpoints, DO rate-limit; calculate-tax and mapkit-token are the two that do not.

surface: helpr:// custom scheme — the stated trust boundary in Info.plist and deepLinkRoute.ts
claim: The app is SAFE here today, but for reasons other than the ones written down, and the written reason would license an unsafe change. Info.plist says of the helpr scheme: 'Registering it here is also the trust boundary: this scheme is only deliverable to this bundle, which is why src/lib/deepLinkRoute.ts is allowed to route it without the https host allowlist.' deepLinkRoute.ts:80-86 repeats it: 'the scheme is only deliverable to us because it is registered in our own Info.plist, which is the same trust boundary the allowlist provides for https links.' That is not what a custom URL scheme is. Registration controls who RECEIVES helpr:// — it places no restriction whatsoever on who may SEND one. Any installed app can call UIApplication.open on helpr:///..., and any web page in any browser can navigate to it. So it is emphatically NOT equivalent to the https host allowlist, which constrains the sender. What actually keeps this safe is two things neither comment mentions: (a) the /auth/* and /admin path guards at deepLinkRoute.ts:118-120 run AFTER the scheme branch, so they still apply to helpr URLs, and (b) every reachable destination re-reads server state under RLS rather than trusting the URL — I verified the highest-value one, PaymentSuccess.tsx, which ignores params for its verdict entirely and polls jobs.payment_status, resolving to held / not_held / unknown, firing its success haptic only on a confirmed 'held' and performing no writes. A hostile helpr:///payment-success?job_id=<someone else's> therefore hits RLS, reads nothing, and lands on 'unknown'. FILED BECAUSE the stated boundary is the kind a future change leans on: anyone adding a helpr:// route that trusts a query parameter would be doing so on the authority of a comment that is wrong. Fix is to correct both comments to name (a) and (b) as the real controls.
repro: Read the CFBundleURLTypes comment in ios/App/App/Info.plist (the com.Helpr.nativereturn dict) and src/lib/deepLinkRoute.ts:80-86; both assert sender-side exclusivity. Then src/lib/deepLinkRoute.ts:88 'if (!isNativeReturnScheme && !ALLOWED_DEEP_LINK_HOSTS.has(url.host)) return null' — the allowlist is skipped for the scheme while :118-120 guards still run. Then src/pages/PaymentSuccess.tsx:240-280: the confirm effect selects budget/category/payment_status from jobs by id and sets state from HELD_STATUSES / NOT_HELD_STATUSES, with :283-290 gating the haptic on isHeld; no write anywhere in the file. deepLinkRoute.test.ts:207 already exercises a helpr: URL.

Item 3 ('Cold-start push tap') is listed as unsettled on the grounds that the evidence is 'a read of node_modules' showing only 'retainUntilConsumed: true and a replay when a JS listener attaches'. surface: iOS app-switcher snapshot — chat, payments, earnings and ID documents are captured unredacted by default
claim: The privacy shield that redacts the iOS app-switcher snapshot only runs for users who have opted into the app lock, so by default the snapshot captures whatever screen the user was on. AppLockGate's appStateChange handler ends with 'if (isAppLockEnabled() && userRef.current) setCovered(true)', and the pause handler opens with 'if (!isAppLockEnabled() || !userRef.current) return'. isAppLockEnabled() reads safeStorage for APP_LOCK_ENABLED_KEY === '1' and returns FALSE when unset, and the only writer is the Profile > Security toggle (SecurityTab.tsx:297). So the default for every account is an unredacted snapshot. That matters more here than in a typical app because iOS writes those snapshots to disk under the app container and they persist across termination, and the screens in question are an open chat thread, payout and earnings figures, and the ID-document upload surface. The usual bar for an app handling money and identity documents is to redact unconditionally, which is what banking apps do precisely because the setting cannot be relied on. The mechanism is already built and correct — it is simply behind an opt-in most people will never find. PRECISE FIX, cheaper than it looks: the snapshot is taken around backgrounding, so gating the shield on the 'pause' event alone (rather than on appStateChange) covers it for everyone WITHOUT reintroducing the Control-Centre / notification-shade flash the current design was rewritten to avoid — that flash is the appStateChange path, and the header comment explains at length why it was made conditional. Only the isAppLockEnabled() check on 'pause' needs to drop. NOT FIXED BY ME: this is session-privacy and lh-onboarding-auth owns app-switcher redaction.

surface: Live en-route tracking — stops the moment the helper leaves the app, and the poster is not told
claim: Live position sharing is driven by a 45-second setInterval inside the WKWebView (JobTracking.tsx:673), and Info.plist declares only 'remote-notification' in UIBackgroundModes — there is no 'location' background mode. iOS suspends a suspended app's JS timers within seconds of backgrounding, so the interval stops firing as soon as the helper leaves the app. That is not an edge case: it is the single most common thing a helper does after tapping 'on my way' — switch to Apple Maps or Google Maps for driving directions. So the feature works precisely while the helper is staring at Helpr and not driving, and stops while they are driving. The poster is given no signal that it has stopped. JobTracking.tsx:1639 renders 'Updated {toLocaleTimeString}' — an ABSOLUTE clock time with no relative framing and no staleness state — which is the format least likely to be read as stale: nobody computes that 'Updated 10:09' means thirty-two minutes ago. The pin sits at the helper's starting point and reads as current. This is the same defect class the 2026-08-31 fix was written to solve (the comment at :620-624 records a frozen updated_at proven by moving the helper 1.5 km); that fix made the interval exist, but only while foregrounded. RECOMMENDED FIX IS THE CHEAP ONE, NOT THE BACKGROUND MODE: declaring a location background mode invites App Review scrutiny, costs battery, and contradicts this feature's own stated restraint at :627-632 about not tracking someone for a whole job. Instead make the UI truthful — render relative time ('Updated 3 min ago') and show an explicit paused/stale state once updated_at exceeds roughly twice the 45s cadence, so the poster knows the position is not live rather than being quietly misled.

Scope of the effect is :637-641 (helper only, on_the_way only). ios/App/App/Info.plist UIBackgroundModes contains only 'remote-notification' — no 'location'. surface: pro-customer-portal → status semantics on the membership self-serve exit
claim: READ THIS FIRST: this is NOT an authorization bypass. pro-customer-portal correctly refuses an unauthenticated caller - index.ts:20 'if (!authHeader) throw new Error("No authorization header")' and :24-26 reject a bad token - and no billing portal session can be created without a valid user JWT. I probed it with no credentials as part of the sanctioned money-endpoint auth sweep, got a 500 rather than the expected 401, stopped immediately per the orchestrator's rule, and did not probe it again; the 500 turned out to be a status-code defect, not a hole. THE ACTUAL DEFECT: the single catch at :80-86 converts EVERY throw into an opaque 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}, so three completely different conditions are indistinguishable to the client and to monitoring: (1) not authenticated / expired session - should be 401; (2) 'No Stripe customer found' at :50, which is the ROUTINE state for any member who has never subscribed - should be 404 or a 200 with a clear 'no membership to manage'; (3) an actual Stripe or runtime failure - correctly 500. User-facing consequence on a money surface: a member whose session lapsed, and a user who simply has no subscription, both click 'Manage membership' and are told the server broke. The second case is not an error at all. Observability consequence: genuine Stripe outages are buried in a stream of 500s generated by routine auth and no-customer cases, which matters more than usual given EF-008 - the cron-side alerting that would otherwise notice a 500 spike is itself unprovisioned. This function is the OUTLIER among its siblings: create-payment answers 401 {"error":"Missing authorization header"} and stripe-connect answers 401 {"error":"Not authenticated"} to the identical probe. That is the same drift the file's own comment at :35-40 describes for a different bug - 'Both siblings were fixed; this one was not.' Minor secondary point: req.json() is awaited at :19 BEFORE the auth check at :20, so an unauthenticated request's body is parsed before it is rejected. Not exploitable (it is .catch()-guarded and nothing is done with the value before auth) but the ordering is backwards. Fix is small and entirely in my lane: throw typed errors or return early with the right status, and let the catch handle only the genuinely unexpected.
repro: Live prod, no credentials, empty body, single request, not repeated: curl -X POST https://fncmgoasalhdgfwzhsqa.supabase.co/functions/v1/pro-customer-portal -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' -> HTTP 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}. CONTROLS from the same sweep, same method, showing this is an outlier and not the project convention: create-payment -> 401 {"error":"Missing authorization header"}; stripe-connect -> 401 {"error":"Not authenticated"}; release-payout -> 401 (gateway); auto-release-payment, process-scheduled-payouts, void-cancelled-payments, charge-recurring-visits, money-reconciliation, cleanup-abandoned-accounts -> 401 'Unauthorized'; send-notification-email, send-push-notification -> 401 {"error":"Unauthorized"}. Auth enforcement confirmed by reading, not assumed: index.ts:20 and :24-26 both reject before any Stripe call at :48.
evidence: live HTTP 500 body quoted above plus the ten 401 controls from the same unauthenticated sweep; supabase/functions/pro-customer-portal/index.ts:19 (body parsed before auth)
:80-86 (the catch that flattens all three to 500)

Every one of the other 21 SQL-only crons is registered, so this is a one-off omission and not a design gap. The other 21 SQL-only crons all return true with gaps from 00:30:00 to 30:00:00. The equivalent query over the 22 function-backed crons returns registered=true for all 22. Job detail: SELECT command, count/max from cron.job_run_details -> command ' SELECT public.extend_boosts_with_no_applications(); ', 2916 runs, 0 with status <> 'succeeded', last_start 2026-09-02 18:00:00.155184Z. Monitoring dependency confirmed by reading pg_get_functiondef(sweep_dead_crons): its WITH expected AS (SELECT ... FROM public.cron_work_expectations c WHERE c.expected_max_gap IS NOT NULL) is the sole source of jobs it will consider.

claim: 43% of all notifications IGNORE the user's notification preferences. claim: auto-tip-charge resolves the poster's Stripe customer with customers.list({email, limit:1}) and gives up with 'no_saved_card' if that ONE record has no card — but one email routinely holds several Stripe customer records and only one carries the saved card. CONFIRMED against live prod, with exact numbers and a sharper consequence than originally filed. THE GAP IS EXACTLY ONE: prod has 44 active cron.job rows and 43 cron_work_expectations rows; the anti-join (cron.job LEFT JOIN cron_work_expectations WHERE e.jobname IS NULL) returns precisely one row — extend-boosts-hourly, schedule '0 * * * *', active=true. 'It is SQL-only rather than net.http_post' is NOT the explanation: the other SQL-only crons (reap-stranded-instant-payouts, sweep-expired-auto-bans, sync-profiles-update-grants) are all registered. It was simply missed. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSED EXTENSION: extend_boosts_with_no_applications() gives each paid boost exactly ONE chance to be extended. Its eligibility window is bounded on BOTH sides — 'boost_expires_at > now() AND boost_expires_at <= now() + interval 1 hour' — and it is idempotent-guarded by boost_auto_extended=false. The cron ticks hourly, so exactly one tick ever falls inside a given boost's final hour. Miss that single tick and boost_expires_at moves into the past, the row can never satisfy 'boost_expires_at > now()' again, and there is no catch-up pass anywhere. So one missed hour permanently destroys the 12-hour make-good on every boost expiring in it, the poster keeps paying $3 (BOOST_FEE_CENTS) for a boost that got no applications and no extension, and nothing anywhere reports it. Combined with SC-001 (the Pro free-boost ledger being client-writable) the boost feature is the weakest link in this lane. claim: If localStorage access throws (Safari 'Block All Cookies', WKWebView/embedded-browser storage disabled, enterprise/kiosk policy), React NEVER MOUNTS. Two unguarded module-scope reads on the boot path: (1) @capgo/capacitor-social-login's oauth-popup-bridge.js:53 shouldAutoFinishOAuthRedirect(), auto-run on import and pulled in eagerly by the static import at src/lib/socialAuth.ts:15; (2) src/integrations/supabase/client.ts:26 'storage: Capacitor.isNativePlatform() ? keychainStorageAdapter : localStorage'. The user gets index.html's #boot-loader forever with no error, no retry, no message. Identical failure in Chromium AND WebKit. Everything downstream is already guarded (safeStorage.safeGet), so the whole failure is those two lines.
repro: Dev server on :5231 off origin/main b170609a. Playwright addInitScript defines window.localStorage as a throwing getter (DOMException SecurityError), which is what Safari 'Block All Cookies' does. Chromium: MOUNTED=false, root children=1, root innerText length=0, #boot-loader still visible, pageerror 'The operation is insecure.'. WebKit: identical (MOUNTED=false, boot-loader visible). Control (clean storage): MOUNTED=true, textLen=658, boot-loader gone. LAYERED PROOF via .audit-scratch/boot-layers.mjs, which serves real localStorage only to allowlisted stack frames: allow=[index.html:294] -> dies at shouldAutoFinishOAuthRedirect, MOUNTED=false. allow=[index.html:294, twitter-provider] -> dies at src/integrations/supabase/client.ts:26:74, MOUNTED=false. allow=[index.html:294, twitter-provider, supabase/client.ts] -> 21 further accesses all absorbed by safeStorage.safeGet, MOUNTED=TRUE, textLen=658. So exactly two sites are fatal and guarding both is sufficient. Sibling cases all boot fine: corrupt non-JSON session, half-written session, expired garbage session, quota-full (setItem throws), indexedDB blocked.

claim: The client and the server disagree about which timezone a job's scheduled start is in, and the disagreement gates a trust/safety control. note: PATCH PROPOSED (not shipped — owner review). Scope split: the money lane owns create-payment action=tip; this lane owns the AUTO-tip duplicate and the copy. THE THREE EDITS. (1) supabase/functions/auto-tip-charge/index.ts:348 currently 'const feeCents = stripeProcessingCostCents(tipCents)' and passes it as application_fee_amount on a PaymentIntent whose amount is tipCents — so the fee is taken OUT of the tip. Replace with the gross-up: charge amount = tipCents + feeCents where feeCents is the fixed point f >= stripeProcessingCostCents(tipCents + f), keep application_fee_amount = feeCents, and leave transfer_data.destination unchanged so the helper's transfer nets exactly tipCents. NAIVE ADDITION IS WRONG and is the trap: stripeProcessingCostCents(tipCents) understates the cost of the LARGER charge, so tipCents + stripeProcessingCostCents(tipCents) leaves the platform ~1 cent short at most amounts. posterFees.ts:72-75 already solves this exact fixed point ('let floorCents = Math.ceil((base * STRIPE_PCT + STRIPE_FLAT_CENTS) / (1 - STRIPE_PCT)); while (floorCents > 0 && floorCents < stripeProcessingCostCents(base + floorCents)) floorCents++'). claim: verification-webhook is unreachable by every vendor that is supposed to call it. surface: Direct offer expiry → expire_pending_direct_offers poster notification
claim: When a direct offer expires the poster is almost never told, because the notification window is 5 minutes wide but the sweep that opens it runs once an hour. expire_pending_direct_offers flips direct_offer_status to 'expired' in a CTE, then — instead of notifying from that CTE's RETURNING rows — re-queries public.jobs with 'direct_offer_expires_at > now() - interval 5 minutes'. Its only caller is the auto-expire-jobs edge function, on cron jobid 16 schedule '0 * * * *'. So of the 60 minutes in which an offer can lapse, only the last 5 before a run land inside the notify window: roughly 55 of every 60 expirations set the status and send NOTHING. The poster is left waiting on an offer the platform has already killed, with no signal that it is now open to everyone. The fix is to notify from the CTE that did the update rather than re-deriving the set from a time window — the RETURNING clause already selects id, customer_id, offered_to_helper_id and title, and is discarded.

claim: The saved-search anti-spam throttle is applied to the DIGEST path as well as the immediate-notification path, so a digest-mode helper can receive at most one matching job per saved search per hour in a digest that is only sent once a day. The matching query filters on 'AND (s.last_notified_at IS NULL OR s.last_notified_at < now() - interval 1 hour)', and the loop body stamps last_notified_at = now() for every contributing search BEFORE branching on digest_mode. On the digest branch the helper is not notified at all — the match is parked in match_digest_queue for daily-match-digest to drain — yet the hour-long throttle is spent all the same. A second matching job posted 10 minutes later does not match the search, so it never reaches the queue and never appears in the digest. Throttling exists to stop notification spam; a daily digest is already the batching mechanism, so applying the same throttle to it silently drops matches the helper explicitly asked to be told about. The stamp belongs on the immediate branch only.

Urgent jobs bypass digest_mode but NOT the throttle.

claim: Signup's hardest failure shows the user a raw backend string. (src/lib/authErrors.ts:13-15) — but Signup.tsx does not call it; ResetPassword.tsx:116 does. So the good copy exists and the signup screen cannot reach it. Flagged --blocker not for the copy alone but because the underlying quota is a launch-capacity question nobody has answered: this is the auth email budget shared by signup confirmations, password resets AND resends, and it is reachable in ordinary use.

claim: The Supabase session is NOT in the iOS Keychain, despite the file, the export and the call site all being named 'keychainStorageAdapter'. It is in NSUserDefaults. client.ts:36 reads 'storage: Capacitor.isNativePlatform() ? keychainStorageAdapter : localStorage', which reads as 'Keychain on device, localStorage on web'. The adapter actually writes through @capacitor/preferences, and that plugin's own iOS source is unambiguous: Preferences.swift:19-20 'private var defaults: UserDefaults { return UserDefaults.standard }', with get/set/remove going straight to it (:39-48). So the access token AND the long-lived refresh token are written to (a) localStorage, readable by any script that executes in the WKWebView, and (b) an unencrypted plist in the app container, which is included in unencrypted iTunes/Finder and iCloud backups and is NOT protected by device-passcode-gated Keychain accessibility. The adapter's own header comment says 'Mirror auth-token writes to NSUserDefaults' and cites 'NSUserDefaults survives Offload App + reinstall' as a FEATURE — that same property means uninstalling the app does not clear the refresh token. I am reporting the naming as the primary defect rather than the storage choice: localStorage is Supabase's documented default and the mirror exists for a real, well-documented reason (WebKit evicting localStorage under memory pressure). The problem is that the name asserts a security property the code does not have, which is precisely what stops anyone noticing. Scope note, stated rather than assumed: I inventoried what is stored and found the session tokens only — no card, bank or government-ID material is written to either store by this adapter.
repro: 1) Read src/integrations/supabase/client.ts:34-39 — storage is keychainStorageAdapter on native. 2) Read src/integrations/supabase/keychainStorageAdapter.ts in full — line 2 imports { Preferences } from '@capacitor/preferences'; setItem (:92-98) and removeItem (:99-105) call Preferences.set/remove; getItem (:88-91) falls back to localStorage. There is no Keychain API anywhere in the file and no @capacitor-community/keychain-style dependency. 3) Verified against the PLUGIN'S OWN SOURCE rather than its docs, per the audit standard: node_modules/@capacitor/preferences/ios/Sources/PreferencesPlugin/Preferences.swift:18-20 defines the backing store as UserDefaults.standard, and :39/:43/:47 route get/set/remove to it. NOT VERIFIED BY ME: I did not dump the on-device plist or a device backup to observe the token at rest — the iOS platform component is not installed on this machine, so the storage location is established from the plugin's source, not from a filesystem read.
evidence: 87-105 (and its own header at :4-7 naming NSUserDefaults); node_modules/@capacitor/preferences/ios/Sources/PreferencesPlugin/Preferences.swift:18-20

note: MIGRATION FEASIBILITY (asked by orchestrator): a bare ADD CONSTRAINT CHECK (start_time < end_time) WOULD FAIL on live data — it must repair first, in the same migration. Measured on prod: helper_availability holds 14 rows, of which exactly 1 violates start_time < end_time (id 036f02c0-0d5e-438c-9277-d36e686e16b6, helper lexilombas05@gmail.com, day_of_week 0, 21:00:00 -> 17:00:00, is_available TRUE). Also measured, because the same migration should carry them: 0 duplicate (helper_id, day_of_week, specific_date) groups, so a UNIQUE on that triple applies cleanly TODAY and would additionally make the '7 rows per helper' invariant real (it is currently unenforced, and HelperAvailability.handleSave's delete-then-insert is the thing that used to duplicate rows — see ST-003); 0 rows with day_of_week outside 0..6; 0 NULL start/end times; 0 rows with specific_date set at all, so the date-override path is entirely unexercised. RECOMMENDED ORDER in one replay-safe migration: (1) repair the single row — swapping to 17:00->21:00 is the only repair that preserves both endpoints the user actually chose, versus resetting to the 09:00-17:00 default which silently discards them, or setting is_available=false which silently removes a day; (2) ADD CONSTRAINT CHECK (start_time < end_time) NOT VALID then VALIDATE, so the failure mode is visible rather than a hard abort; (3) optionally the UNIQUE. Guard every step with IF NOT EXISTS / to_regclass per CLAUDE.md replay-safety, and prove with 3 consecutive PGlite applies. NOTE the repair targets the OWNER's own account, so it is his call whether 17:00-21:00 is what he meant.

claim: RW-005 RESOLVED: a fresh signup arriving as approval_status='approved' is INTENTIONAL, not an approval-queue bypass. complete-signup sets approval_status:'approved' unconditionally on every success path (index.ts:464-465) under an explicit design comment: 'Auto-approve — there is no manual admin review step anymore... Identity verification + payout setup happen later as separate Stripe-gated steps.' The column default 'pending' and the RLS INSERT policy (profiles 'Users can insert their own profile', WITH CHECK includes approval_status='pending') are the trigger-inserted starting state; the edge function is what flips it. So the gate is real and it is auto-approve by design. BUT the more useful statement is the one RW-005 and OA-001 only make together, and it is bigger than either: APPROVAL IS A SIDE EFFECT OF AN EDGE FUNCTION THAT CAN SILENTLY NOT RUN. There is no reconciliation sweep, no retry and no alert behind it — when complete-signup does not execute, the account simply stays at the default forever and ProtectedRoute.tsx:334 bounces it. That is the same single point of failure as the missing legal consent in OA-001. SECOND, DEPENDENT FINDING: because auto-approve is the design, /account-pending's copy is fiction for essentially every account that reaches it. It says 'We are verifying your details' and 'Hang tight, {name}. Our team is reviewing your credentials' (AccountPending.tsx:270,278-279), renders a 'Final admin review' checklist step (:198), and quotes a staffed SLA 'during business hours' (:328-329). No such review exists. A user who lands there — which now only happens when complete-signup silently failed — is told to wait for a team that will never look at their account, so the one screen that should surface the OA-001 breakage instead reassures them into waiting indefinitely.
repro: Code: supabase/functions/complete-signup/index.ts:461-465 (the unconditional approved write and its design comment). claim: The SIGNED_OUT handler that wipes the persisted React Query cache is registered INSIDE a try whose catch is empty, AFTER five dynamic imports and two analytics init calls. If any of those fails — most commonly an ad blocker refusing the PostHog chunk, which uBlock Origin, Brave and Safari content blockers all do by default — supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange is never registered, so queryClient.clear() and removePersistedClient() never run on sign-out. The previous user's entire persisted cache survives in IndexedDB under 'helpr-rq-cache' for the full 24h PERSIST_MAX_AGE_MS and is rehydrated by the next person to open the app on that device. The auth token IS removed from localStorage either way, so the app looks completely signed out and nothing signals the leak. The leaked payload is exactly what queryClient.ts's own header comment says must not survive sign-out. This is the fail-open-catch class: the comment '/* analytics + error tracking must never break the app */' is true of its intent but the block it guards also contains the privacy control.
repro: Worktree off origin/main b170609a, dev server :5231, real authed session for seeded test poster helpr-audit-web-0824@mailinator.com (user id e977a30f-7065-4e75-8498-dba435ac2044). Loaded /dashboard, interacted to trigger the deferred init, read IndexedDB keyval-store['helpr-rq-cache'], called supabase.auth.signOut(), waited 4s, re-read. CONTROL (analytics loads): before = 73743 bytes / 13 queries / user id present; AFTER = 88 bytes / 0 queries / user id ABSENT — wipe works. BLOCKED (route.abort('blockedbyclient') on any URL matching /posthog/i, which is what an ad blocker does): before = 73743 bytes / 13 queries; AFTER = 73743 bytes / 13 queries / user id STILL PRESENT, byte-identical — the wipe never ran. Leaked query keys include ["currentUser","e977a30f-..."], ["dashboardContext",...], ["dashboardJobs",...], ["proTier",...], ["dashboardJobsCount",...] and ["pif-count","e977a30f-...","helpr-audit-web-0824@mailinator.com"] — so the prior user's EMAIL ADDRESS and user id are among the persisted values. claim: Query retries are exponential but have NO JITTER, so a Supabase blip makes every client in the field retry in lockstep. The QueryClient sets a custom retry() predicate but never sets retryDelay, so TanStack v5's default applies: Math.min(1000 * 2**attemptIndex, 30000) — deterministic 1s then 2s, identical on every device. Combined with refetchOnWindowFocus:true, a brief outage produces a synchronised 3x request spike aimed at the service that just failed. Bounded rather than dangerous (retry caps at 2 attempts and mutations are explicitly retry:0), which is why this is LOW and not a blocker — but the app already knows the right shape: src/lib/realtimeRecovery.ts:238-247 jitters its own backoff with 'base + Math.floor(Math.random() * 400)' and the file's header comment calls jitter out by name as a requirement. The two backoff policies in the codebase disagree with each other, and the React Query one is the one facing the whole user base.
repro: Static, verified by exhaustion against the tree at origin/main b170609a: 'grep -rn retryDelay src/' excluding tests returns ZERO hits, so nothing overrides the library default anywhere. src/lib/queryClient.ts:33-42 defines retry() only. TanStack Query v5's documented default retryDelay is Math.min(1000 * 2 ** attemptIndex, 30000) with no randomisation. Contrast src/lib/realtimeRecovery.ts:57 (RETRY_DELAYS_MS) and :238-247, which add Math.random()*400 of jitter on top of its schedule.

surface: public.scan_message_content() BEFORE INSERT ON messages · public.is_caller_banned()
claim: The off-platform-contact scanner's repeat-offender auto-suspension is a COMPLETE NO-OP, and it tells the user they are suspended while they are not. On the 3rd flag in 24h the trigger runs 'UPDATE profiles SET auto_suspended_until = now() + interval 7 days' and sends a notification titled 'Account temporarily suspended'. It never sets ban_status. But is_caller_banned() — the only thing enforce_ban_gate consults, and it gates messages, jobs, applications and every other write — tests 'ban_status IN (banned, temp_banned, permanently_banned)' and treats auto_suspended_until ONLY as a modifier on an already-temp_banned row. So ban_status stays 'active', the gate returns false, and the user keeps messaging, posting and bidding for the full 7 days they were told they were suspended. Second-order: sweep_expired_auto_bans() requires ban_status='temp_banned', so it never clears the stale auto_suspended_until either — the column stays dirty forever. This is the platform's primary anti-disintermediation enforcement and it does not enforce.
repro: PROD fncmgoasalhdgfwzhsqa, proven by evaluating the real predicates against the exact state each writer leaves, no mutation. is_caller_banned()'s predicate applied to ('active', now()+7d) — the state scan_message_content leaves — returns FALSE. The same predicate applied to ('temp_banned', now()+7d) — the state BanDialog.tsx:213 leaves — returns TRUE. sweep_expired_auto_bans()'s predicate applied to ('active', now()-1d) returns FALSE, so the stale column is never lifted. Sources: pg_get_functiondef for scan_message_content, is_caller_banned, enforce_ban_gate, sweep_expired_auto_bans; pg_get_triggerdef showing messages_scan_content BEFORE INSERT ON public.messages and trg_ban_gate_messages using enforce_ban_gate. claim: One offence, two independent consequence ladders that do not know about each other and disagree on every parameter. (A) The server trigger scan_message_content writes a fraud_flags row and escalates on a 24-HOUR rolling count, 2 rungs, ending in an auto_suspended_until write that does nothing (see AM-008). (B) The client-invoked RPC apply_message_violation_consequence writes a user_violations row and escalates through apply_consequence_ladder on an ALL-TIME count, 3 rungs (warning / final_warning / pending_ban_review + 7-day suspension), and does set ban_status. Both fire for the SAME blocked message: sendHandlers.ts:200 calls logViolation() which invokes (B), while the INSERT that follows trips (A). So a single message costs the user one fraud flag AND one violation, counted in two different windows toward two different ceilings. The lh-audit standard calls a duplicated ladder a drift hazard even when the copies match; these do not match. Note this also DISPROVES the obvious worry: the scanner is NOT client-only — scan_message_content is a genuine BEFORE INSERT trigger, so a user calling the messages API directly is still flagged and hidden. What they escape is only ladder (B).

surface: iOS app-switcher snapshot redaction — AppLockGate.tsx / appLock.ts
claim: App-switcher snapshot redaction is coupled to an OPT-IN setting that is not about snapshots, and that setting is OFF by default — so for the default user the iOS task-switcher preview captures whatever is on screen: an open chat thread, a checkout/payment screen, a profile, a payout account. AppLockGate DOES implement a wordless privacy shield and correctly binds it to Capacitor's appStateChange (iOS willResignActive), which is the right event — it fires before the system snapshot, and the file's comments show real care in separating it from the 'pause' event that arms the actual lock (AppLockGate.tsx:239-255). The gate is also mounted above every route (App.tsx:645-676), so nothing escapes it. The defect is the guard on the last line of that handler: 'if (isAppLockEnabled() && userRef.current) setCovered(true)' (:253). isAppLockEnabled() reads safeStorage 'helpr_app_lock_enabled' === '1' and returns false when the key is ABSENT, and false again on any storage error (appLock.ts:147-155) — so it is default-OFF and fails to OFF. App Lock is separately opt-in behind a biometric confirmation (SecurityTab.tsx:290). These are two different threat models being served by one flag: App Lock answers 'someone picked up my unlocked phone', snapshot redaction answers 'what is visible in the app switcher and written to the snapshot cache on disk'. A user who never enables App Lock has no reason to expect the second is disabled too, and the snapshot persists in the container. Apps handling messaging, payment or identity data normally redact unconditionally. RECOMMEND: raise the shield on resign-active whenever a user session exists, independent of isAppLockEnabled() — the isBiometricPromptOpen() carve-out at :253 already prevents the flash-over-own-dialog bug that guard was partly protecting.
repro: 1) src/components/AppLockGate.tsx:245-255 — the appStateChange handler returns early on isActive, skips the biometric-sheet case, then gates setCovered(true) on isAppLockEnabled(). 2) src/lib/appLock.ts:147-155 — isAppLockEnabled() is 'safeStorage.getItem(APP_LOCK_ENABLED_KEY) === "1"' with APP_LOCK_ENABLED_KEY = 'helpr_app_lock_enabled' (:66); an absent key is false, and the catch returns false, so the default state is off. setAppLockEnabled removes the key entirely when disabling (:161), so 'off' is genuinely 'absent'. 3) CORROBORATED ON A REAL INSTALL, not just read: the app installed on the booted simulator (com.Helpr, CFBundleVersion 5906, device 10492853-2555-4C57-8542-F555BCEA9865) has 29 CapacitorStorage.* keys in its NSUserDefaults plist — helpr_onboarding, helpr_last_auth_method, helpr_post_count, the sb-*-auth-token, and so on — and 'helpr_app_lock_enabled' is NOT among them. So on that actual instance App Lock is off and the shield would not raise. NOT VERIFIED BY ME: I did not background the running app and visually inspect the captured task-switcher snapshot. The conclusion is from the handler's own guard plus the observed absence of the enabling key, not from a screenshot of the app switcher. Someone should confirm visually before this is closed.
evidence: 147-161; src/components/profile/SecurityTab.tsx:290; plutil -p over <DataContainer>/Library/Preferences/com.Helpr.plist on sim 10492853-2555-4C57-8542-F555BCEA9865 showing 29 CapacitorStorage.* keys with no helpr_app_lock_enabled

claim: RW-004's missing mechanism: an awaited promise that NEVER SETTLES between account creation and the profile write. fileToBase64() attaches only onload and onerror. FileReader has THREE terminal events — load, error and abort — so an aborted read resolves nothing and rejects nothing, and the await hangs forever. This is the FIRST await inside completeProfile (Signup.tsx:241), and completeProfile runs AFTER supabase.auth.signUp has already created the account. Every consequence matches RW-004's evidence exactly: the auth user exists (account created); supabase.functions.invoke('complete-signup') is never reached, so the function is never ENTERED and writes no edge_rate_limit_log row — which is precisely the dispositive absent artifact lh-onboarding-auth used to prove it was never invoked; the catch at Signup.tsx:398 never runs, so there is no report() and no toast (no error); the finally never runs, so setLoading(false) never fires and the button spins forever; and the profile keeps only what handle_new_user inserted (user_id, full_name, email), leaving phone, location, date_of_birth and avatar_url blank — exactly the four fields RW-004 names. Intermittent because it depends on the image and the device. A SECOND path produces byte-identical evidence: supabase.functions.invoke is called with no AbortSignal and no timeout anywhere in the signup path, so a stalled connection on a flaky mobile network hangs the same way with the same silence. Note the avatar is a HARD requirement of the signup form ('Add a profile photo' blocks submit), so every single signup passes through fileToBase64. The codebase already learned this exact lesson elsewhere and did not apply it here: keychainStorageAdapter.ts's HARD CAP comment says verbatim 'The try/catch below is NOT sufficient on its own. It catches a REJECTION; it does nothing for a Capacitor bridge call that never settles at all.'
repro: Worktree off origin/main b170609a, dev server :5231. Imported the app's OWN module through the Vite graph (import('/src/pages/signup/signupHelpers.ts')) and raced fileToBase64 against a timeout. CONTROL, ordinary 4-byte File: 'RESOLVED'. ABORT, FileReader subclassed so readAsDataURL schedules this.abort() on the next tick, 2MB File: 'NEVER_SETTLED' after 4000ms — neither resolved nor rejected. HANDLER PROBE, FileReader subclassed with setters spying on which handlers the promise assigns: ['onload','onerror'] — onabort is never attached. Separately, 'grep -rn "AbortSignal|abortSignal|signal:|timeout" src/pages/Signup.tsx src/pages/signup/' returns no timeout on the invoke path, and 'grep -rn "onabort" src/' returns zero hits app-wide (the only .abort() in src/ is useMapKitJs.ts:133, which pairs it with a timeout — so the pattern is known in this codebase, just not applied here). Harness: ~/.lh-audit/lh-concurrency-cache/.audit-scratch/never-settles.mjs

MECHANISM FOUND by lh-concurrency-cache (CC-006) and INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED by me. It slots onto the absent-artifact proof rather than replacing it. fileToBase64 (src/pages/signup/signupHelpers.ts:70-78) builds a Promise around a FileReader and attaches ONLY onload and onerror. FileReader has three terminal events; an ABORTED read fires onabort, which nothing listens for, so the promise neither resolves nor rejects — it hangs forever. I re-read the function and confirmed: reader.onload and reader.onerror only. 'grep -rn onabort src/' returns ZERO hits app-wide, so this is not a one-off omission. That await is the FIRST statement of completeProfile (Signup.tsx:241), which runs AFTER auth.signUp has already created the account irreversibly. Every symptom I documented from prod falls out of that one line: the auth user exists; functions.invoke('complete-signup') is never reached, so the handler is never entered and NO edge_rate_limit_log row is written — which is exactly the absent artifact I used as dispositive proof; the catch at Signup.tsx:398 never runs, so no report() and no toast; the finally never runs, so setLoading(false) never fires and the button spins forever; and the profile holds only what handle_new_user inserted, i.e. precisely the four fields RW-004 named, because they are the PAYLOAD of the call that never fired. SEVERITY RISES, not falls: this is not a rare race but a deterministic hang on a path EVERY user walks — the avatar is a hard requirement of the form ('Add a profile photo' blocks submit, Signup.tsx:131-134) — whose probability depends only on the file and the device. SECOND UNGUARDED PATH, must be fixed with the first or the intermittency merely moves: supabase.functions.invoke is called with no AbortSignal and no timeout at Signup.tsx:252 AND at CompleteProfile.tsx:400 (verified by grep). A stalled connection on a flaky mobile network hangs identically — and CompleteProfile is the RECOVERY path for this very failure, so the recovery can hang the same way. THE FINDING BEHIND THE FINDING: this codebase already learned this lesson and did not apply it here. src/integrations/supabase/keychainStorageAdapter.ts:21-26 says verbatim that a try/catch 'catches a REJECTION; it does nothing for a Capacitor bridge call that never settles at all', and adds a 2000ms hard cap for exactly this shape — while zero onabort handlers and two untimed invokes sit on the highest-traffic path in the funnel. surface: prod GoTrue auth config (fncmgoasalhdgfwzhsqa) — signup confirmation / password reset / resend
claim: ANSWERS OA-003. Two separate questions, two different answers. (1) SENDER: custom SMTP is NOT configured, but it does not matter — auth mail does NOT go through Supabase's built-in sender. A GoTrue Send Email Hook is wired to the auth-email-hook edge function, which sends via Resend on the verified apex domain louisianahelpr.com. So the 'built-in sender is not for production' deliverability blocker does NOT apply. (2) THROUGHPUT: the blocker is real and is a config value, not a sender. GoTrue applies rate_limit_email_sent BEFORE it invokes the hook, so the hook never gets the chance. That limit is EXACTLY 2 emails per hour, project-global, on a FIXED clock-hour window — Supabase's built-in-sender default, left unraised when the hook was added. At launch the platform can confirm at most 2 new signups per hour in total, shared with every password reset and resend; the 3rd user in any clock hour gets a 429 and no email. FIX IS CONFIG-ONLY, NO CODE: raise Auth > Rate Limits > 'Rate limit for sending emails' in the Supabase dashboard (or PATCH rate_limit_email_sent via the Management API). Nothing in the repo needs to change. This also RESOLVES the anomaly OA-003 could not explain ('one rolling hour 03:40-04:05 carried 4, so it is not a flat 2/hour'): the window is fixed, not rolling — 2 landed at the end of hour 03 (03:40:52, 03:40:54) and 2 at the start of hour 04 (04:04:09, 04:05:56). Four in 25 minutes, still exactly 2 per clock hour.

surface: prod platform_settings.min_supported_build — ForceUpdateGate / native force-update lever
claim: The force-update gate has never been armed and is the ONLY remote lever that can retire a broken native build. Live prod: platform_settings.min_supported_build = 0 AND latest_build = 0, updated_at 2026-05-02, updated_by NULL — never touched by an operator. 0 is the documented GATE_OFF value (src/lib/minSupportedBuild.ts), so the gate is fully disabled. WHAT VALUE IT NEEDS: the build number of the FIRST TestFlight build cut from a commit at or after 6d3cf8f19 (2026-09-01, 'Every APNs action button the server has ever sent was dropped on the floor'), which is the first commit whose AppDelegate posts .capacitorDidRegisterForRemoteNotifications. Fastlane's next_build_number takes max(TestFlight)+1 and the last delivered build was 7101, so that build will be >= 7102. Set min_supported_build to that exact number the moment it ships — not before, or the gate locks out every existing install with no replacement available to update to. WHAT BREAKS UNTIL THEN: every build <= 7101 in the wild — which is EVERY build that exists, since no build containing the APNs fix has ever been produced — silently drops the APNs token iOS hands it on every launch. push_tokens never fills; those users receive zero push notifications, forever, with no error, no log and no prompt to update. Because the gate reads 0 they are never turned away, so they keep running the broken binary indefinitely. This compounds NB-004 (lh-native-bridge): the fix exists in main and has never been in a build anyone has run, and the one mechanism that could force those users off it is switched off. Note the gate correctly fails OPEN on every read failure by design (minSupportedBuild.ts) — that is right and must not be changed; the defect is purely that the value was never set.

claim: An internal developer utility that solicits an Apple Sign In .p8 PRIVATE KEY is publicly reachable and crawlable on the production marketing domain. public/tools/apple-jwt.html is copied verbatim into dist/ by the build and is live at https://www.louisianahelpr.com/tools/apple-jwt.html (HTTP 200, 10415 bytes). It renders a form whose fields are Team ID, Key ID, Services ID and a textarea labelled 'Private Key (.p8 contents)' with the instruction 'Paste the entire contents including BEGIN/END lines', then produces a client-secret JWT for Supabase Auth. IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT, verified not assumed: the page does NOT exfiltrate. It contains ZERO network calls — no fetch, no XMLHttpRequest, no sendBeacon, no <form action>, no dynamic .src — the signing is done entirely in-browser with WebCrypto. So this is not a live credential leak and I am not filing it as one. The real harms are (a) robots.txt does not Disallow /tools, so a page on the company's own domain reading 'paste your Apple private key here' is indexable, and (b) it hands a phisher a ready-made harvester: clone the page to a lookalike domain, add one fetch(), and it inherits the provenance of having genuinely been served from louisianahelpr.com. An App Review or security-conscious visitor finding it also reads badly on a marketplace asking users to trust it with money. It has no reason to be on the production web surface at all — it is a one-time setup tool.

surface: helpr:// deep links / the native Stripe return — dead whenever the app was opened from the home screen
claim: OBSERVED ON DEVICE, reproducible: the appUrlOpen listener never delivers when the app process was started WITHOUT a URL — which is every normal launch from the home screen. Deep links are then dead for the entire life of that process. Controlled experiment on the iOS 26.1 simulator, app built from origin/main: terminate, plain 'simctl launch' with no URL, settle 25s, then 'simctl openurl helpr:///legal?tab=privacy'. Result: the app foregrounds and stays on the guest browse feed, and error_logs receives ZERO rows from the HelprApp user agent after the marker timestamp. That zero is the proof the handler never ran, because handleIncomingUrl's FIRST act on a helpr: URL is 'await Browser.close()', which on this device always rejects with 'No active window to close!' and is reported to error_logs by the catch at nativePush.ts. Whenever the handler runs, that row appears. Contrast, same build, same session: after cold-launching the app FROM a URL, two subsequent warm URLs both navigated correctly (a guest was bounced to /login with 'That page needs an account' and the destination preserved) and each produced its browserClose row at 22:05:35 and 22:05:43. Tally: 5 failures in the launched-without-URL condition, 3 successes in the launched-with-URL condition. WHY THIS IS A BLOCKER: the production Stripe flow is exactly the failing condition. The user opens the app from the home screen (no URL), taps Pay, Browser.open() presents SFSafariViewController, Stripe redirects to the native=1 page, that page fires helpr:///payment-success — and nothing happens. No Browser.close(), no navigation. The user is stranded looking at the website inside a sheet they must dismiss by hand, which is precisely the defect nativeReturnBounce.ts was written to eliminate. MECHANISM — HYPOTHESIS, NOT OBSERVED: useNativePushSetup guards on a MODULE-level 'listenersAttached' flag but tracks cancellation in an effect-local 'cancelled' variable, and its deps are [navigate]. If the effect re-runs once (plausible on a plain launch, where NativeLaunchRouter navigates from '/' to the default route and changes router state), the cleanup sets cancelled=true on run 1 while run 2 returns immediately at the listenersAttached guard; run 1 then hits 'if (cancelled) return' and never reaches either App.addListener('appUrlOpen') or App.getLaunchUrl(). Launching WITH a URL would avoid the extra navigation and let the chain finish. Someone should confirm that before fixing.
repro: Build origin/main, install on the booted iOS 26.1 sim. FAILING: xcrun simctl terminate booted com.Helpr; xcrun simctl launch booted com.Helpr; sleep 25; xcrun simctl openurl booted 'helpr:///legal?tab=privacy'; then query prod error_logs for created_at > <marker> and user_agent like '%HelprApp%' -> 0 rows, and the screenshot shows the unchanged guest feed (~/lh-audit-shots/nb-scheme-7-controlled-warm.png). PASSING: xcrun simctl terminate; xcrun simctl openurl booted 'helpr:///legal?tab=terms' (cold launch FROM the url) -> lands exactly on Legal with the Terms pill selected (~/lh-audit-shots/nb-scheme-5-coldlaunch-url.png); then two warm openurls -> both navigate and both log browserClose rows.
