claim:
CONSENT CAPTURE, stated separately from the data loss in OA-001 because it has a different owner and a different remedy. A live auth account exists whose holder ticked BOTH the "I am 18 or older" attestation and the "I agree to the Terms, Privacy Policy and Platform Rules" checkbox, and neither was ever persisted. helpr-audit-routewalker@mailinator.com (auth.users 9a31db25-5089-4789-8adf-e5c737586166, created 2026-09-02T18:18:42Z, email CONFIRMED at 18:21:52Z, signed in at 18:41:36Z) has terms_version_accepted='' (empty string, not the 'Jun 2026' its successful sibling carries), terms_accepted_at NULL, accepted_terms_at NULL and ZERO rows in legal_acceptances. The app told this person their agreement was recorded; it has no record of it. On a real-money, 18+-gated marketplace that is a compliance gap, not a data-quality one: if this user later disputes a charge, is injured on a job, or turns out to be a minor, the platform cannot produce the consent it asserted at signup.

The structural cause is that consent is written by a SECOND, unguarded network call. auth.signUp() creates the account irreversibly; every profile field, the approval flip AND the entire legal record then depend on a separate supabase.functions.invoke('complete-signup') that has no retry, no queue, no compensating write and no reconciliation sweep. Nothing anywhere notices when it does not happen.

lh-verification-credentials independently established the same mechanism from the other side and it is worth stating as one sentence, because neither lane could say it alone: complete-signup/index.ts:465-470 sets approval_status='approved' UNCONDITIONALLY once validation passes ("Auto-approve - there is no manual admin review step anymore"), handle_new_user inserts without it, and the profiles INSERT policy hard-pins 'pending' so it cannot be forged. So 'pending' is purely the pre-completion state, and APPROVAL TO USE THE PLATFORM IS A SIDE EFFECT OF AN EDGE FUNCTION THAT CAN SILENTLY NOT RUN - the same single point of failure that loses the consent record also decides whether the account is approved. RW-005 is therefore NOT an approval-queue bypass (it is intentional) but it confirms this finding's mechanism.
repro: Live prod fncmgoasalhdgfwzhsqa, read-only. (1) SQL join of auth.users -> public.profiles -> legal_acceptances for helpr-audit-routewalker@mailinator.com returns terms_version_accepted='', terms_accepted_at NULL, accepted_terms_at NULL, legal_acceptances count 0, approval_status='pending'; the sibling account helpr-audit-routewalker2@mailinator.com created 5 minutes later through the identical form returns terms_version_accepted='Jun 2026' and approval_status='approved'. (2) The consent is only ever written by complete-signup: Signup.tsx:266-276 sends ageAttested + termsAccepted in the invoke body and NOTHING else in src/ writes terms_version_accepted or legal_acceptances on the signup path. (3) complete-signup was never entered - its first action is checkRateLimit (index.ts:25-30) which INSERTs an edge_rate_limit_log row on EVERY invocation, allowed or denied, and there is no bucket='complete-signup' row anywhere near 18:18:4x (rows exist at 18:23:42, 18:24:13 and 18:40:52). (4) I then REPRODUCED the loss mechanism end to end against the real form - see the reproduction recorded on OA-001 and finding OA-008: interrupting the window between auth.signUp resolving and the complete-signup POST completing leaves exactly this state, and the double-submit race proposed in OA-002 is NOT the cause (disproven - the winning submission still invokes).

claim: The bundle-size gate weighs 38 KB of a 913 KB first-paint graph and reports 'within budget'. It has been measuring 0.6% of the shipped JavaScript. Its extraction is INITIAL_CHUNKS=grep -oE 'assets/[^"]+\.js' dist/index.html, documented in its own comment as 'entry + modulepreload'. But dist/index.html contains ZERO modulepreload links, because vite.config.ts:401-403 sets modulePreload: { resolveDependencies: () => [] } — a deliberate, reasonable perf choice (documented at vite.config.ts:398-403) that returns an empty dependency list so Vite emits no <link rel=modulepreload> at all. The two files are in direct conflict and neither references the other. Result: the grep matches exactly ONE file, the entry chunk at 38 KB. The author anticipated this exact failure and wrote an EMPTY-GREP GUARD (bundle-size.yml:113-131) whose comment even names the cause — 'a plugin rewrites the script tags (this repo already has THREE transformIndexHtml plugins in vite.config.ts rewriting the head)' — but the guard only fires on ZERO matches. One match satisfies it, so the check passes having weighed almost nothing. This is the guard-that-cannot-fail shape: MAX_INITIAL_KB=1500 is compared against 38, and MAX_CHUNK_KB=400 is applied to that single file only, so a 390 KB chunk (jspdf.es.min-DKS1p-*.js is 390 KB today) entering the initial graph would never be flagged. NOT CURRENTLY OVER BUDGET — the true graph is 913 KB against a 1500 KB budget, so nothing is broken for users today; the defect is that the gate would keep saying 'within budget' all the way past 1500 KB. Fix is to derive the initial graph from the entry chunk's static-import closure rather than from index.html markup, or to assert a minimum plausible chunk COUNT rather than merely non-zero.
repro: Fresh npm run build at origin/main 1f00d28b2 in an isolated worktree (EXIT=0). grep -c modulepreload dist/index.html -> 0. The gate's own extraction, run verbatim: grep -oE 'assets/[^"]+\.js' dist/index.html | sort -u -> exactly one line, assets/index-DGGXrC9M.js, 38 KB; INITIAL_TOTAL=38, budget 1500 -> PASS. True first-paint cost, computed by walking the entry chunk's STATIC import closure (static  only, dynamic imports excluded): 77 chunks totalling 913 KB, led by supabase 204 KB, react-vendor 130 KB, proxy 119 KB, tanstack 66 KB, lucide 58 KB. 913/38 = 24x more than the gate weighs. Whole-bundle context: dist/assets JS+CSS = 6.2 MB across 393 chunks.
evidence: gate extraction reproduced verbatim -> 1 chunk / 38 KB vs measured static closure 77 chunks / 913 KB
.github/workflows/bundle-size.yml:101 (INITIAL_CHUNKS grep) and :113-131 (empty-grep guard that only fires on zero)

claim: Recognition is inferred by comparing a returned string against a COPY LITERAL, so rewording one sentence silently breaks the social sign-in error path with nothing failing. friendlyProviderError needs to know whether friendlyAuthError actually matched the raw provider error, or whether it fell through to its generic default. friendlyAuthError cannot answer that — it must return a string, so it reports 'here is something to show' and 'I recognised this' with the same value. The workaround is an equality test against the fallback SENTENCE: 'if (mapped === "Couldn't sign you in — give it another try?")'. The day anyone rewords that fallback — a copy pass, a tone change, swapping the em dash, fixing the curly apostrophe (the lh-audit standard explicitly calls for curly quotes, so this string is a live target) — the comparison stops matching. Nothing throws, no test fails, no type error: the branch simply never fires again, and every UNRECOGNISED Apple/Google failure silently starts showing the bare 'Couldn't sign you in' instead of the provider-named line the function exists to produce. It fails by going quiet, which is the same class as everything else this sweep has surfaced. THE FIX IS NOW TRIVIAL and that is why this is filed rather than left as a comment: matchAuthError(raw): string | null landed in authErrors.ts as part of the OA-003 fix (ffbb94f49) and separates recognition from presentation. friendlyProviderError becomes 'return matchAuthError(raw) ?? providerFallback', deleting the literal comparison entirely. NOT FIXED BY ME: the social flow is outside the scope the orchestrator approved for the OA-003 fix; queued for the fix phase.
repro: Read src/lib/socialAuth.ts:87-96 at origin/main. The function body is: const raw = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err ?? ''); if (!raw) return provider-named fallback; const mapped = friendlyAuthError(raw); if (mapped === "Couldn't sign you in — give it another try?") { return provider-named fallback; } return mapped;. The compared literal must stay byte-identical to authErrors.ts's GENERIC_SIGN_IN_FALLBACK — including the em dash and the typographic apostrophe — and nothing enforces that coupling: no shared constant, no test, no type. Confirmed the coupling is undefended: a grep over src for test files referencing the string "Couldn't sign you in" returns 0 hits, so no test would catch a reword. The function's own comment at :91-92 acknowledges the mechanism ('friendlyAuthError returns the generic fallback for unrecognised input') without noting that it is a string-equality coupling across two files. Post-fix state confirmed: authErrors.ts now exports matchAuthError returning null on no match, verified by a runtime table (matchAuthError('nope') === null), so the replacement is a one-line change with no new machinery.
evidence: src/lib/socialAuth.ts:87-96; src/lib/authErrors.ts:22-25 (GENERIC_SIGN_IN_FALLBACK) and :25-47 (matchAuthError) as landed in ffbb94f49; grep for "Couldn't sign you in" across src/**/*.test.* returning 0 hits

note: OWNER DECISION, framed as two options with their costs. This is a product call, not a bug fix — the code does what it was written to do; the question is whether one opt-in flag should govern two different threat models. App Lock answers 'someone picked up my unlocked phone'. Snapshot redaction answers 'what is visible in the app switcher, and what is written to the snapshot cache on disk'. A user who declined the first has no reason to believe they also declined the second. ---- OPTION A (RECOMMENDED): always shield on resign-active whenever a user session exists. Delete isAppLockEnabled() from the single guard at AppLockGate.tsx:253, leaving 'if (userRef.current) setCovered(true)'. COST: one line. The shield is wordless, opaque and aria-hidden, and comes straight back down on the isActive branch (:246-248), so a signed-in user sees a brief opaque panel in the app switcher and nothing else changes — no new prompt, no new setting, no lock. The isBiometricPromptOpen() carve-out immediately above it (:253) already prevents the flash-over-your-own-dialog bug that this guard was partly protecting, so the risk that guard was covering is already covered by its neighbour. RISK: a signed-in user who genuinely wants to see their own content in the app switcher loses that; nobody has asked for it. This is what apps handling messaging, payment or identity data normally do. ---- OPTION B: split the setting in two — keep App Lock opt-in, add a separate 'Hide screen in app switcher' preference, default ON. COST: a new stored preference, a new row in the security tab, new copy, and a migration story for existing installs (an absent key must read as ON, or every current user stays unprotected — which is exactly the default-off trap being fixed). More surface, more to get wrong, and it asks the user a question most cannot meaningfully answer. ---- WHY NOT 'LEAVE IT': the default is not neutral. isAppLockEnabled() reads a key that is ABSENT by default and its catch also returns false (appLock.ts:147-155), so the shield is off for every user who has not deliberately turned App Lock on, and off again for anyone whose storage read fails. Corroborated on the real install: the app on the booted simulator has 29 CapacitorStorage.* keys and helpr_app_lock_enabled is not among them. ---- STILL OWED regardless of which option is chosen: nobody has backgrounded the running app and LOOKED at the captured task-switcher image. The conclusion rests on the handler's guard plus the observed absence of the enabling key, not on a screenshot. Whoever takes this should confirm visually first — the sim is available and the app is installed.

FRAMING THE ORCHESTRATOR ASKED TO BE MADE EXPLICIT: THE RECOVERY PATH CARRIES THE SAME DEFECT AS THE THING IT RECOVERS FROM. When completeProfile hangs at signup, the product's answer is that the user confirms their email, logs in, and is routed to /complete-profile to finish the job. That screen calls supabase.functions.invoke('complete-signup') at CompleteProfile.tsx:400 with NO AbortSignal and NO timeout — the identical untimed call as Signup.tsx:252. So the designated remedy for a silent hang can hang silently in exactly the same way, and a user who was stranded once can be stranded again by the screen built to un-strand them, with the same absence of any error. That is why this closes as three fixes or none: (1) fileToBase64's missing onabort (signupHelpers.ts:70-78), (2) the untimed invoke at Signup.tsx:252, (3) the untimed invoke at CompleteProfile.tsx:400. Fixing only (1) and (2) leaves the recovery path hanging on a flaky mobile connection; fixing only (1) moves the intermittency from the file reader to the network. Note also that CompleteProfile is reached by EVERY social-login user by design (Apple/Google never collect phone, DOB, city or avatar), not just by signup-failure casualties — so path (3) is on the primary onboarding route for social sign-ups, not an edge case.

claim:
At the single worst moment in the funnel the user is shown a raw Supabase SDK internal string. When the complete-signup invoke fails on the network - i.e. exactly when the auth account has just been created irreversibly and the profile, the approval flip and the entire legal record are about to be lost - the toast reads, verbatim: "Failed to send a request to the Edge Function". That is the supabase-js FunctionsFetchError message. It names an internal component ("Edge Function"), does not say what failed from the user's point of view, does not say their account WAS created, and offers no next step.

This is the SAME defect class as OA-003 but a different string on a different path, so fixing OA-003 does not fix it: userFacingError() (src/lib/userFacingError.ts:37-57) has no INTERNAL_PATTERNS entry matching "Edge Function", and the string is 44 chars so the 160-char length gate passes it through as human copy.

The state it leaves behind is what makes this HIGH rather than a copy nit. Measured: the user is returned to /signup with the form still populated and the Create Account button ENABLED, while a live, email-confirmable auth account for that address already exists in prod with no profile, no approval flip and no legal_acceptances row. The only affordance offered is to press Create Account again - which now takes the already-registered branch at Signup.tsx:337-347 and redirects them to /login telling them the address is already registered. The recovery path from a failure that stranded their account is to be told the account they just failed to create already exists.

Toast captured by 100ms DOM polling of [data-sonner-toast] - a MutationObserver missed it, and a post-hoc read is useless because sonner auto-dismisses in ~4s, which is why an earlier run of this same probe wrongly recorded "no toast". biometricGate.ts:42-43 reads checkBiometry() and returns true when info.isAvailable is false. Verified against the PLUGIN OWN iOS SOURCE rather than its docs: BiometricAuthNative.swift:38 computes isAvailable from canEvaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics) - BIOMETRICS ONLY. biometryLockout is the one that inverts the security property. claim:
The iOS app-switcher privacy shield never engages for the default user, because it is gated on an unrelated OPT-IN setting. AppLockGate does implement snapshot redaction, and implements it thoughtfully - but all three of its lifecycle handlers are guarded by isAppLockEnabled(), and that setting is off unless the user has explicitly turned on the Face ID app lock in Profile -> Security.

AppLockGate.tsx:245-253 is the appStateChange handler - the willResignActive hook, and the ONLY thing that can cover the screen before iOS takes its snapshot - and it covers only when isAppLockEnabled() and a user are both true. AppLockGate.tsx:257-262 (pause) returns early on the same condition. appLock.ts:147-155 returns true only when safeStorage holds helpr_app_lock_enabled === "1", a key written solely by setAppLockEnabled(true) from the Security tab and absent on every fresh install.

So for a signed-in user who has not opted into the app lock - the default, and the overwhelming majority - backgrounding the app lets iOS capture whatever was on screen into the task-switcher snapshot, which is written to disk in the app container and persists in the recents carousel: an open chat thread, the payout or cash-out screen, a dispute with its evidence, another user profile, or a job street address.

The coupling looks unintended rather than deliberate, and that is the argument for changing it. The lock and the shield are two different mechanisms with two different costs: the LOCK is intrusive - it raises a biometric prompt - and making it opt-in is right. The SHIELD is a free opaque overlay for the ~200ms of backgrounding, and there is no user-facing reason to withhold it from anyone. The file own header at :31-46 already describes them as separate concerns and explains at length why appStateChange must never lock; the same reasoning argues it should always shield. Recommended: gate covering on the presence of a signed-in user alone, and keep isAppLockEnabled() on the pause/resume LOCK decision only.
repro: Source-established, and I am flagging the limit rather than papering over it: the guard and the default are proven from source, but I did NOT capture an iOS task-switcher snapshot - the iOS platform tooling is not installed on this machine, so the observable artifact (a recents-carousel screenshot showing a chat thread) is not in hand. What IS proven: (1) AppLockGate.tsx:245-253 and :257-262 read in full, both guarded by isAppLockEnabled(). (2) appLock.ts:147-155 returns safeStorage.getItem(APP_LOCK_ENABLED_KEY) === "1"; APP_LOCK_ENABLED_KEY is helpr_app_lock_enabled at :66; the only writer is setAppLockEnabled at :157-166, called from the Security tab. Nothing seeds it, so it is absent by default and isAppLockEnabled() is false on a fresh signed-in install. (3) setCovered is therefore never called for a default user on any lifecycle event. Handing the device-side snapshot capture to lh-native-bridge, per this lane brief.

claim:

ResetPassword.tsx:79-80 does: parse window.location.hash, and if type === "recovery" then setReady(true). That is a synchronous check on an attacker- or user-supplied fragment; it does not wait for, or consult, the token exchange. claim:
The TOTP shared secret is written to the system clipboard and nothing ever clears it. TwoFactorCard.tsx:288 does navigator.clipboard.writeText(data.secret) from the setup-key button.

What makes this worth raising rather than a routine copy affordance is that it is no longer a fallback. The comment at :270-276 records that the owner removed every QR code from the app on 2026-08-25 and that the setup key is now "the primary control ... rather than a fallback under the image". So copy-to-clipboard is the main enrolment path, and essentially every user who turns on 2FA puts their TOTP seed on the pasteboard.

A TOTP seed is not a one-time code - it is a permanent credential that mints valid codes forever. On iOS the general pasteboard persists until something overwrites it, is readable by the app the user switches to next, and syncs to their other Apple devices over Universal Clipboard. So the secret that exists to be the second factor sits in the least private buffer on the device, indefinitely, immediately after the user was told to paste it somewhere. Anyone who reads that pasteboard later - another app, another synced device - holds a permanent bypass of the 2FA the user just enabled.

Proportionate fix, in preference order: keep the copy affordance (it IS the enrolment path now) but bound its lifetime - on native, write through Capacitor Clipboard and schedule a clear, since UIPasteboard supports an expirationDate and the app already owns the native layer; at minimum clear the clipboard when enrolment completes or the card unmounts, and say in the copy that the key was copied and will be cleared. Offering a tap-to-reveal-and-type path alongside it would remove the need entirely for users who want it.

Also inventoried while here and NOT a concern: the app three other clipboard writes are a support case number (ReportDialog.tsx:259), a referral link (CompletionPrompts.tsx:113) and the user own message text (messages/MessageActionSheet.tsx:85). None is a credential.

(2) src/components/profile/TwoFactorCard.tsx:285-291 read in full: the onClick awaits navigator.clipboard.writeText(data.secret) inside a try/catch and sets a 1500ms "copied" flag; there is no clearing write anywhere in the file, and no unmount cleanup. note: CORRECTION to the root cause, found by building. The dev server and the production bundle have DIFFERENT fatal sets, and the originally-proposed fix did not work at all against dist/. (1) In the BUNDLE, @capgo/capacitor-social-login is NOT on the eager path — Rollup splits it into a lazily-loaded chunk, so shouldAutoFinishOAuthRedirect never runs at boot. The dev server serves unbundled modules eagerly, which is the only reason it was the first offender there. The single fatal site in dist/ is the bare localStorage identifier reaching assets/client-*.js (src/integrations/supabase/client.ts:26). (2) More importantly, the fix I proposed — 'import "./lib/storageFallback"' as the first import in main.tsx — is correct by ES semantics, DID fix the dev server, and STILL FAILED against the bundle: MOUNTED=false, unchanged. Rollup inlines a small side-effect module into the ENTRY CHUNK BODY, and an entry chunk body runs only after every chunk it imports has already been evaluated. The offending reads live in those vendor chunks, so they ran first no matter where the import was declared. Only an inline script in index.html is guaranteed to execute before any module chunk — which is exactly why the existing pre-paint theme script is inline rather than imported. The shipped fix is therefore in index.html, above the theme script, and touches NO file that collides with lh-onboarding-auth. This is a textbook instance of CLAUDE.md's rule that a result measured on the dev server is not a result; had this not been built, a fix that measured clean in dev would have shipped with the blocker fully intact.

LEAD WITH THE MONEY CONSEQUENCE — this is why it is a blocker rather than a deep-link bug. THE PRODUCTION STRIPE FLOW IS THE FAILING CONDITION: home screen -> Pay -> Browser.open() presents SFSafariViewController -> Stripe -> helpr:///payment-success -> NOTHING HAPPENS. The person has paid and is stranded inside a sheet they must dismiss by hand, with the app behind it unaware the payment occurred. That is the exact defect nativeReturnBounce.ts was written to eliminate, and it is reintroduced by the delivery step rather than by the bounce. THE PROOF METHOD, stated explicitly because it is the load-bearing part: I did not argue from 'the screen did not change', which cannot distinguish 'did not navigate' from 'navigated somewhere that looks similar'. I used an artifact that appears WHENEVER the handler runs and showed its ABSENCE. Every helpr: URL makes handleIncomingUrl call 'await Browser.close()' as its first act; on a simulator that always rejects with 'No active window to close!' and the catch reports it to error_logs with tags.source=nativeReturn.browserClose. Contrast on the SAME build in the SAME session: 5 failures in the launched-without-URL condition, every one with ZERO rows; 3 successes in the launched-with-URL condition, every one WITH the row (22:05:35Z, 22:05:43Z, and the cold launch at 22:04:05Z). An absent artifact whose presence is otherwise reliable. SEQUENCING, must be honoured: fix NB-017 BEFORE NB-001. Fixing NB-001 (stripe-connect not tagging native=1) changes nothing on its own because the delivery step downstream is dead; if both are fixed together the wrong one gets credited. MECHANISM REMAINS A HYPOTHESIS AND MUST NOT BE TREATED AS THE CAUSE: the module-level listenersAttached guard against the effect-local cancelled variable is plausible and UNPROVEN. Whoever fixes this confirms the mechanism first — a hypothesis presented as a cause is how the wrong fix ships and gets credited.

TWO FACTS THAT BELONG NEXT TO EACH OTHER IN THE ROLLUP, and an ordering constraint from lh-notifications. (1) DEVICE-CONFIRMED: the binary actually installed on the audit simulator was built Aug 28 21:09 — before both fixes — and its Louisiana Helpr.debug.dylib contains ZERO of the AppDelegate category identifiers while its only occurrence of capacitorDidRegisterForRemoteNotifications is the PLUGIN'S OWN rejection string ('event capacitorDidRegisterForRemoteNotifications not called. Visit ...'). The build I made from origin/main contains all eight identifiers (APPLY, SAVE, REPLY, VIEW, OPEN_THREAD, JOB_APPLY, MESSAGE, JOB_ACCEPTED) plus the notification name. Same command, same file type, opposite results — a negative with a positive control. So an installed binary demonstrably drops the APNs token and carries the plugin's own 'not called' string as the only trace. (2) ORDERING — N-002 (lh-notifications) MUST LAND BEFORE min_supported_build IS RAISED. The 32 accounts with no notification_preferences row currently bypass push_enabled AND the category gate entirely, because fan_out_push_on_notification wraps its whole gate in 'IF prefs.user_id IS NOT NULL'. That is harmless ONLY because push_tokens holds zero rows — which is this finding confirming itself from the other side. The moment a build carrying ad315368 ships and real tokens arrive, those 32 accounts start receiving push they never consented to. So the release sequence is: land N-002, then ship the build, then raise min_supported_build to retire the token-dropping builds. Raising the bump first, or shipping before N-002, converts this finding into a consent problem.

claim:
The email-to-social identity-linking path has NEVER been exercised, on a launch where both providers are live and prominent. Across all 40 prod auth users there are ZERO accounts with more than one identity (auth.identities grouped by user_id, max = 1), and the only providers that have ever produced an identity are apple and email - Google has produced none, despite being offered as one of two buttons on both /login and /signup.

So the collision this lane brief asks about - "an existing email-account collision is handled rather than creating a duplicate profile" - has no evidence either way in production. The scenario is ordinary: a user signs up with email and password as alice@example.com, comes back later and taps Sign in with Apple, and Apple returns the same address. Whether GoTrue links that identity to the existing user or creates a SECOND user with the same email is decided by project-level auth configuration, which this codebase neither sets nor reads and which is not exposed through the Supabase MCP tools available to me. It is the same shape as OA-006: a behaviour the app depends on, promises nothing about, and does not control.

The consequence if it links WRONG is not cosmetic on this app specifically, because of how signup is built. A second auth user means a second handle_new_user profile row that never went through complete-signup - so it lands with approval_status pending, terms_version_accepted empty and zero legal_acceptances, which is precisely the stranded state of OA-001/OA-009, and it would then be bounced into the /account-pending dead end filed as OA-017. Today prod is clean (0 duplicate lower(email) in auth.users, 40 users to 40 profiles, 1:1), so nothing is broken right now - this is an untested path, not an observed defect, and I am filing it as a pre-launch gap rather than a bug.

What IS verified working, so it is not re-audited: both providers are genuinely enabled and configured at GoTrue - authorize?provider=google returns 302 to accounts.google.com with a real client_id and the correct supabase /auth/v1/callback redirect_uri, and provider=apple returns 302 to appleid.apple.com with client_id com.Helpr.sign... - and Sign in with Apple is present and rendered FIRST on both screens, which is what Apple HIG asks for (SocialAuthButtons.tsx:55-79). Cancel is handled as a distinct outcome rather than an error (socialAuth.ts:28,66-82,146).
repro: Live prod fncmgoasalhdgfwzhsqa, read-only SQL plus unauthenticated HTTP. (1) One aggregate query returned: dup_auth_emails 0, auth_users_total 40, users_with_multiple_identities 0, identity_providers "apple, email", dup_profile_user_ids 0, profiles_total 40, unconfirmed_auth_users 2. The zero on users_with_multiple_identities is the finding: no account has ever linked a social identity to an existing one, so the path is unexercised. (2) curl -D - on GET /auth/v1/authorize?provider=google and ?provider=apple against the prod project both return HTTP 302 with Location headers to the real IdP carrying a populated client_id and redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Ffncmgoasalhdgfwzhsqa.supabase.co%2Fauth%2Fv1%2Fcallback - so neither provider is a dead button. (3) NOT VERIFIED BY ME, stated rather than assumed: I did not drive an actual Apple or Google sign-in, because that needs real IdP credentials I do not hold, and I could not read the GoTrue linking setting - it is project auth config, not reachable through the Supabase MCP tools. Recommend the owner settle it before launch with one manual test: sign up with email, then sign in with Apple on the same address, and check whether auth.users gains a row.
evidence: SQL aggregate over auth.users/auth.identities/public.profiles on prod (0 multi-identity users
email); curl -D - /auth/v1/authorize?provider=google and ?provider=apple both 302 to real IdP; src/components/auth/SocialAuthButtons.tsx:55-79; src/lib/socialAuth.ts:28

claim: The only unguarded zero-row write in the entire admin console, on a LIVE product surface. remove() runs supabase.from('broadcast_messages').delete().eq('id', id), inspects ONLY error, and then unconditionally splices the row out of the React Query cache with qc.setQueryData. A delete that matched zero rows returns { data: [], error: null } — indistinguishable from success — so the admin watches the broadcast vanish from the list while it is still live in the database and still being served to every signed-in user by BroadcastBanner. The UI confirms the lie. Fix is the house pattern already used 8 lines up in this same file: .select('id') passed through unwrapMutation() from src/lib/mutationResult.ts, which AdminBroadcasts.tsx:104 (cancel) already does.
repro: Verified independently, two ways. (1) Static: I swept every .update()/.delete() call site under src/components/admin/** and src/pages/Admin.tsx for a missing .select(). Three candidates came back; two are false positives that are not database writes at all — AdminExceptionQueue.tsx:150 is next.delete(id) on a JS Set (its real write at :162 has .select('id') plus a hand-rolled '!updated || updated.length === 0' guard), and AdminJobs.tsx:163/:177 are URLSearchParams.delete and Set.delete. That leaves AdminBroadcasts.tsx:165 as the ONLY one, confirming a delegated sweep that reached the same answer. (2) Live: the surface renders and is real — /admin?view=broadcasts shows 'Scheduled Broadcasts | An in-app banner shown to every signed-in user until it expires | New Broadcast | Nothing scheduled'. NOT DRIVEN: I did not delete a broadcast, because prod has zero broadcast_messages rows and the standing constraint forbids acting on rows I did not create.
evidence: same file); src/lib/mutationResult.ts unwrapMutation; ~/.lh-audit/admin-shots/admin-broadcasts.png; prod SQL confirming broadcast_messages exists with RLS enabled and the fan-out cron is active

EVIDENCE UPGRADED from source-only to a disk artifact, and I am correcting my own filing: I originally wrote that the iOS platform tooling was not installed on this machine. That was FALSE - it was inherited from another lane stating it, which PROTOCOL calls a lead, not a fact. The simulator is booted with the app installed (LH-Audit-iPhone17Pro-261, UDID 10492853-2555-4C57-8542-F555BCEA9865, com.Helpr).

Driven: xcrun simctl launch com.Helpr, waited 8s, captured the foreground screen, then backgrounded the app by launching Safari, then listed the container. iOS wrote snapshots to Library/SplashBoard/Snapshots/sceneID:com.Helpr-default/ - TWO full-resolution .ktx files of 342,091 bytes each plus a downscaled/ pair, all timestamped at the moment of backgrounding. The directory was EMPTY immediately before. So the snapshot is really taken and really persisted to disk in the app container, and at 342KB it is a content-bearing capture, not a blank or covered frame.

Scoped honestly, twice over. (1) The screen captured was the signed-OUT guest job feed, so the snapshot content itself is not sensitive - I did not sign into the simulator build and background a chat thread or the payout screen, so I have NOT captured a snapshot containing private data. What this artifact proves is the MECHANISM: backgrounding persists an unredacted capture of whatever is on screen, and setCovered is the only thing that could change that. The claim that it never fires for a default user remains established from source (AppLockGate.tsx:245-253,257-262 + appLock.ts:147-155), and a signed-out user is covered by the same guard - userRef.current is null - so the code path is identical. (2) The installed simulator build is CFBundleVersion 5906, not necessarily current with origin/main; the guard should be re-read against the shipping build before the fix is verified.
